Nowcasting with mgcv

Source: vignettes/articles/2_nowcasting_mgcv.Rmd
2_nowcasting_mgcv.Rmd

TL;DR

This is a longer article explaining the workings and the choices behind the GAM nowcasting model and its advantages and limitations.

Why nowcasting_mgcv()

nowcasting_mgcv() fits the same nowcasting model as nowcasting_inla(), a negative binomial model for the delay triangle with smooth effects for time and delay, but as a generalised additive model (GAM) with mgcv instead of INLA. mgcv is on CRAN and is installed together with nowcaster, so this function works out of the box, which makes it a good choice when INLA cannot be installed or when a fast estimate is needed.

The model

Let Y_{t,d} be the number of cases with onset in week t that were reported with a delay of d weeks. The model is

Y_{t,d} \sim \text{NegBinom}(\lambda_{t,d}, \phi), \qquad \log(\lambda_{t,d}) = \alpha + f_1(t) + f_2(d),

where f_1 and f_2 are penalised thin plate regression splines and \phi is the dispersion parameter, all estimated by mgcv::gam(). The cells of the delay triangle that are not observed yet (t + d beyond the present week) are then predicted. The uncertainty is propagated by sampling 1,000 sets of coefficients from their approximate posterior distribution and, for each set, sampling the unobserved counts from the negative binomial distribution. Summing the observed and sampled counts over the delays gives 1,000 trajectories of the epidemic curve, which are summarised by their median and 50% and 95% intervals.

Non-structured nowcasting

We use the SARI data from Belo Horizonte shipped with the package. The function needs the data set and the names of the onset and report date columns.

library(nowcaster)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

data(sragBH)
now_mgcv <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = sragBH,
                            date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                            date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                            data.by.week = TRUE)
names(now_mgcv)
#> [1] "total" "data"
head(now_mgcv$total)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>    Time dt_event   Median    LI    LS   LIb   LSb
#>   <int> <date>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1    17 2021-12-19    625  621   633    623  627 
#> 2    18 2021-12-26    695  687   707.   692  698 
#> 3    19 2022-01-02    812  801   829    807  817 
#> 4    20 2022-01-09    887  870   910.   881  893 
#> 5    21 2022-01-16    817  800.  845    810  825.
#> 6    22 2022-01-23    629  608   661    622  639

total holds the estimate for each week of onset (dt_event): the Median, the 50% interval (LIb, LSb) and the 95% interval (LI, LS). With data.by.week = TRUE, data holds the delay triangle used to fit the model, from which we get the curve as observed at the time of the last record:

observed <- now_mgcv$data |>
  group_by(dt_event) |>
  summarise(observed = sum(Y, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(now_mgcv$total, aes(x = dt_event)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LI, ymax = LS), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LIb, ymax = LSb), fill = "grey50", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Median, colour = "Nowcasting")) +
  geom_line(data = observed, aes(y = observed, colour = "Observed")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Nowcasting = "black", Observed = "grey50"),
                      name = "") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%V/%y") +
  labs(x = "Week of onset of symptoms", y = "Number of cases") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))

Controlling the estimation window

Three arguments, all in weeks, control which part of the data enters the model:

  • Dmax: the maximum delay considered (default 15). Cases reported later than Dmax weeks after onset are discarded.
  • wdw: the length of the window, counted back from the last onset week, used to fit the model (default 30).
  • trim.data: the number of most recent weeks to drop before fitting (default 0).

A shorter window makes the fit faster and more local:

now_short <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = sragBH,
                             date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                             date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                             Dmax = 10,
                             wdw = 20)
tail(now_short$total)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>    Time dt_event   Median    LI    LS   LIb   LSb
#>   <int> <date>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1    16 2022-02-20    355  322   398.  342    370
#> 2    17 2022-02-27    344  302   402.  329    361
#> 3    18 2022-03-06    368  312.  433   348.   389
#> 4    19 2022-03-13    343  278.  429.  319.   371
#> 5    20 2022-03-20    320  226   435.  284    360
#> 6    21 2022-03-27    267  146   471.  217.   325

Keep Dmax at 9 weeks or more: the smooth for the delay uses 10 basis functions and needs at least as many distinct delays.

Structured nowcasting, by age

Delays differ between age groups, so the model can be fitted with one smooth for time and one for delay per age class. Pass the age column to age_col and choose the age classes with bins_age ("SI-PNI", "10 years", "5 years" or a vector of break points).

method.group.gam selects how the smooths are shared between age classes:

  • "fs" (default): a factor smooth, s(Time, age_class, bs = "fs"), where the curves of the age classes share one smoothing parameter;
  • "by": one independent smooth per age class, s(Time, by = age_class), plus an intercept per age class.
now_age <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = sragBH,
                           date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                           date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                           age_col = Idade,
                           bins_age = "10 years",
                           method.group.gam = "fs")
names(now_age)
#> [1] "total" "age"
head(now_age$age)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 9
#>    Time dt_event   fx_etaria fx_etaria.num Median    LI    LS   LIb   LSb
#>   <int> <date>     <fct>             <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1    17 2021-12-19 1                     1    123   122   126   122   124
#> 2    17 2021-12-19 2                     2     15    15    17    15    15
#> 3    17 2021-12-19 3                     3     20    20    22    20    20
#> 4    17 2021-12-19 4                     4     30    30    31    30    30
#> 5    17 2021-12-19 5                     5     29    29    31    29    30
#> 6    17 2021-12-19 6                     6     68    68    70    68    68

The element age has the estimate for each age class, while total sums the trajectories over the age classes. The age classes are numbered in increasing order of age; with bins_age = "10 years" class 1 is 0–9 years and class 10 is 90 years or more:

age_labels <- c(paste0(seq(0, 80, 10), "-", seq(9, 89, 10)), "90+")

now_age$age |>
  mutate(age_class = factor(age_labels[fx_etaria.num], levels = age_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dt_event, y = Median)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LI, ymax = LS), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~age_class, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Week of onset of symptoms", y = "Number of cases") +
  theme_bw()

Forecasting

Setting K to a positive number adds K weeks beyond the last onset week to the delay triangle, so the model also forecasts cases that have not started yet. Here we cut the data on 4 July 2020, as if we were nowcasting at that date, and forecast two weeks ahead:

srag_2020 <- sragBH |>
  filter(DT_DIGITA <= as.Date("2020-07-04"))

now_forecast <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = srag_2020,
                                date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                                date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                                K = 2)
tail(now_forecast$total, 4)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>    Time dt_event   Median    LI    LS   LIb   LSb
#>   <int> <date>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1    25 2020-06-14  1104.  788. 1602.  988. 1247 
#> 2    26 2020-06-21  1096.  562. 2256   856  1404.
#> 3    27 2020-06-28  1194.  418. 3350.  839  1743.
#> 4    28 2020-07-05  1293   314. 5517.  774. 2148

Because the data set holds every case reported up to 2022, we can compare the estimate with what was eventually observed:

eventually_observed <- sragBH |>
  mutate(dt_event = DT_SIN_PRI - as.numeric(format(DT_SIN_PRI, "%w"))) |>
  count(dt_event, name = "observed") |>
  filter(dt_event >= min(now_forecast$total$dt_event),
         dt_event <= max(now_forecast$total$dt_event))

now_forecast$total |>
  mutate(part = ifelse(Time > max(Time) - 2, "Forecasting", "Nowcasting")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dt_event)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LI, ymax = LS, fill = part), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Median, colour = part)) +
  geom_line(data = eventually_observed,
            aes(y = observed, colour = "Eventually observed")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Nowcasting = "black", Forecasting = "orange",
                                 `Eventually observed` = "red"), name = "") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Nowcasting = "grey50", Forecasting = "orange"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%V/%y") +
  labs(x = "Week of onset of symptoms", y = "Number of cases") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))

The last two weeks are the forecast. Their intervals are much wider, as no case with onset in those weeks had been observed at the time.

Trajectories and trend

With trajectories = TRUE the function also returns the 1,000 sampled trajectories. They can be summarised in other ways, for instance to classify the trend of the curve in the last weeks with slope.estimate.quant() (which needs the lme4 package). It fits a line to each trajectory over the last window weeks and returns 1 if the curve is increasing, 0.5 if probably increasing, 0 if stable or uncertain, -0.5 if probably decreasing and -1 if decreasing:

now_traj <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = srag_2020,
                            date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                            date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                            trajectories = TRUE)
head(now_traj$trajectories)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#> # Groups:   Time, dt_event [6]
#>   sample  Time dt_event       Y
#>   <chr>  <int> <date>     <dbl>
#> 1 1         12 2020-03-15   349
#> 2 1         13 2020-03-22   351
#> 3 1         14 2020-03-29   298
#> 4 1         15 2020-04-05   267
#> 5 1         16 2020-04-12   278
#> 6 1         17 2020-04-19   303
slope.estimate.quant(trajectories = now_traj$trajectories, window = 3)
#> [1] 0
